method_card.title: Mode, Median and Mean for Ungrouped Data
method_card.content:
There are three averages you need to calculate from a raw (ungrouped) list of values. Each measures the “centre” of the data differently, and choosing the right one depends on the shape of the data and the context.

The mode is the value that appears most often. It is the only average that works with non-numerical data (e.g. favourite colour), but it can be misleading if there are two very different values with equal frequency (bimodal data). The mode is not affected by extreme values.

The median is the middle value once the data are ordered from smallest to largest. For \(n\) values where \(n\) is odd, the median is the \(\frac{n+1}{2}\)th value. For even \(n\), it is the mean of the \(\frac{n}{2}\)th and \(\frac{n}{2}+1\)th values. The median is resistant to outliers, making it ideal for skewed distributions (e.g. house prices, salaries).

The arithmetic mean is calculated as \(\bar{x} = \frac{\sum x}{n}\), where \(\sum x\) is the sum of all values and \(n\) is the number of values. The mean uses every data point, so it is the most “mathematically complete” average — but it is pulled towards outliers. If one extreme value is present, the mean can misrepresent the typical value.

Choosing the right average: use the mode for categorical data or when identifying the most common item; use the median when data are skewed or outliers are present; use the mean when data are roughly symmetrical and you want to include all values in the calculation.
steps: Order the data from smallest to largest before finding the median
Identify the mode by counting how often each value appears
Find the median position using \(\frac{n+1}{2}\) for odd \(n\), or average the two middle values for even \(n\)
State which average is most appropriate and explain why in context

exam_context.marks: 2–4 marks (calculation); up to 3 marks for justifying appropriate average in context
exam_context.frequency: Appears on every paper; justification questions are high-frequency in the interpretation sections

worked_examples.question: Find the median of the following values: 3, 9, 5, 7, 1, 5, 8.

steps.label: Step 2 — Find the middle position
steps.content: There are \(n = 7\) values. The median is at position \(\frac{7+1}{2} = 4\).

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: The 4th value in the ordered list is 5. The median is 5.

worked_examples.question: The ages of seven students are: 14, 16, 15, 14, 17, 14, 18. Calculate the mean and mode. Explain which average is more appropriate to represent the typical age.

steps.label: Step 1 — Calculate the mode
steps.content: The value 14 appears three times; all others appear once. Mode = 14.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: The mean (15.4) is more appropriate here because the data are roughly symmetrical, there are no extreme outliers, and the mean uses all seven values. The mode (14) only reflects the most frequent value and would understate the typical age of the group.

worked_examples.question: A dataset of 8 house prices (in thousands of pounds) is: 120, 135, 142, 150, 155, 160, 168, 950. Calculate the mean and median. Explain which is a better measure of the typical house price and why.

steps.label: Step 2 — Calculate the median
steps.content: Data are already ordered. \(n = 8\), so the median is the mean of the 4th and 5th values: \(\frac{150+155}{2} = 152.5\) (thousands).

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: The median (152.5 thousand) is a better measure of the typical house price. The value 950 thousand is an outlier that pulls the mean up to 247.5 thousand, which does not represent the central cluster of houses priced between 120 and 168 thousand. The median is not affected by this extreme value.

bronze.display: Find the mode of this dataset: 4, 7, 2, 7, 9, 3, 7, 4.

misconceptions.message: The mode is the value that appears most often. 7 appears three times; 4 appears twice. The mode is 7.
Always order the data first: 3, 7, 9, 11, 15. The median is the 3rd value (middle of 5) = 9.
Sum = 5+10+15+20+10 = 60. Mean = 60 ÷ 5 = 12. Divide by the number of values (5), not the highest value.

bronze.display: A dataset has 7 values. At which position is the median?

misconceptions.message: Median position = (n+1)/2 = (7+1)/2 = 4. The median is the 4th value in the ordered list.

bronze.display: Find the median of the ordered list: 2, 5, 8, 11.

misconceptions.message: There are 4 values (even n). The median is the mean of the 2nd and 3rd values: (5+8)/2 = 6.5.

bronze.display: Which average is most appropriate for categorical data such as favourite subject?
options: Mode
Median
Mean
Range

misconceptions.message: Only the mode works with non-numerical (categorical) data. You cannot calculate a mean or median of categories like 'History' and 'Maths'.

bronze.display: A dataset is: 6, 6, 7, 8, 9. What is the mode?

misconceptions.message: The mode is the value that appears most often. 6 appears twice; all others appear once. Mode = 6.
Sum = 15. Mean = 15 ÷ 5 = 3. When all values are equal, the mean equals that value.

silver.display: The scores of 9 students are: 45, 62, 38, 62, 71, 55, 62, 48, 90. Find the median.

misconceptions.message: Order first: 38, 45, 48, 55, 62, 62, 62, 71, 90. n=9, median position = (9+1)/2 = 5. The 5th value is 62.

silver.display: Temperatures (°C) over 6 days: 12, 15, 18, 9, 22, 14. Calculate the mean temperature.

misconceptions.message: Sum = 12+15+18+9+22+14 = 90. Mean = 90 ÷ 6 = 15 °C. Make sure you divide by 6, not 5.

silver.display: A dataset contains one very large outlier. Which average would be least affected by this outlier?
options: Mode
Median
Mean
All are equally affected

misconceptions.message: The median is the middle value and is not pulled towards extreme values. The mean uses all data values in its calculation, so a large outlier drags it significantly upward.

silver.display: Five friends earn (per week): £220, £240, £250, £260, £1500. The mean is £494 and the median is £250. Which average better represents their typical earnings? Give the letter of the correct statement.
options: The mean (£494), because it uses all five values
The median (£250), because the £1500 is an outlier that distorts the mean
Both are equally valid
Neither average is useful here

misconceptions.message: The £1500 salary is an outlier. It pulls the mean up to £494, which is higher than four of the five earners. The median (£250) better represents the typical wage in this group.

silver.display: A dataset of 11 values has a sum of 374. What is the mean?
A dataset has mean 20 and contains 5 values. One value is removed and the new mean of the remaining 4 values is 18. What was the removed value?

misconceptions.message: Original sum = 20 × 5 = 100. New sum = 18 × 4 = 72. Removed value = 100 − 72 = 28.

gold.display: Ten values have a mean of 8. A new value of 18 is added. What is the new mean? Give your answer to 1 decimal place.

misconceptions.message: Original sum = 8 × 10 = 80. New sum = 80 + 18 = 98. New mean = 98 ÷ 11 ≈ 8.9 (to 1 d.p.). Check: 98/11 = 8.909…

gold.display: A dataset of 7 values has median 14, mode 11, and mean 15. An 8th value of 25 is added. The dataset is re-ordered. Which statement about the new median is correct?
options: The median stays at 14
The median increases because 25 is above it
The new median is the mean of the 4th and 5th values
The new median equals the old mean

misconceptions.message: With n=8 values, the median position is between the 4th and 5th values. Adding 25 at the top of the ordered list shifts all positions by one — the median is now the mean of the 4th and 5th values.

gold.display: Weekly step counts for a student over 9 days: 4200, 6800, 7100, 5500, 9900, 6800, 7200, 6800, 32000. Calculate the median and the mean (to the nearest whole number). Which is a better representation of typical daily steps?
options: Median (6800), because the 32000 outlier distorts the mean
Mean (about 9589), because it uses all nine data points
Mode (6800), because it appears most often
Both the median and mean give the same result

misconceptions.message: Ordered: 4200, 5500, 6800, 6800, 6800, 7100, 7200, 9900, 32000. Median = 5th value = 6800. Sum = 86300, mean = 86300/9 ≈ 9589. The 32000 value is an extreme outlier that pulls the mean far above the central cluster, so the median is more representative.

gold.display: A dataset has 5 values. Four of them are 3, 7, 9, 11. The mean of all 5 values is 8. What is the fifth value?

misconceptions.message: Required sum = 8 × 5 = 40. Known sum = 3+7+9+11 = 30. Missing value = 40 − 30 = 10.

gold.display: A positively skewed distribution has mean 45, median 38, and mode 30. Which statement correctly explains what 'positively skewed' means for this data?
options: Most values are high; a few extreme low values drag the mean down
Most values are low; a few extreme high values pull the mean upward
The mean, median and mode are all equal
The distribution is symmetrical around 45

misconceptions.message: Positive skew means the tail extends to the right (high values). A few large values pull the mean above the median, which is above the mode. Here mean (45) > median (38) > mode (30) confirms positive skew.
